head2head_summary_note: Commit-then-Steer strictly dominates Native GS, Official PGID-F, and SEAL across matched cohorts and operating points (vs PGID-F: 5.1x faster verify, +16.3pp 9-GS on matched-30, Imprint 0/4 vs 2/4, Reprompt+ 2/108 vs 104/108; vs SEAL: dominates across all 3 40k-calibrated points @12/@4/@2 where SEAL suffers robustness collapse at @12 [9-GS 45.6%, Regen-4 26.3%] and forgery collapse at @4/@2 [Imprint 2/4, Proxy Reprompt 16-26/36, target regen 10-15/18]). Against Paper-faithful SemBind GS-S (matched-20; 4-carrier full matrix incl. GS++ and authors' private training/binding code remain outside released scope), Stage 4D+5B/5C establish a clear architectural Pareto boundary: Commit-then-Steer wins training-free, 3.0x faster gen, 11.7x faster verify, instance-preserving fidelity, zero-shot SDXL/PRC transfer (incl. SDXL Live Imprint 0/4 vs 4/4), AND same-prompt instance-level security (Imprint hyb 1/4, sscd64 2/4 vs SemBind 4/4 BA=1.0000; Same-Prompt Reprompt+ hyb 2/24, sscd64 9/24 vs SemBind 24/24), whereas SemBind GS-S retains higher harsh-occlusion 9-GS survival (93.9% vs 81.7%), higher strong diffusion-regeneration joint survival (80/80 vs 65/80; Commit-Steer 192b auth is 80/80), and 0/72 cross-prompt Reprompt+ at >181/256.
evaluation_policy: Unchanged published top-venue author attacks only; full budgets; no adaptive or improved attacks; independent null calibration and evaluation; report achieved FPR and absolute TPR.
